finding.claim: deleteAccount calls canDelete but discards its boolean result, so any authenticated non-admin user can delete any account by id.
finding.source: Path parameter id of DELETE /accounts/{id} (AccountService.java:19-20); caller User u supplied by caller. Precondition: authenticated non-admin user.

trace.note: deleteAccount(User u, long id) accepts caller and target id
Account a = accounts.get(id) loads any account
canDelete(u, a) called; boolean result discarded, nothing thrown

finding.guards_checked: canDelete (AccountService.java:9-11) has correct admin-or-owner logic but is not enforced; assertCanDelete (13-17) would throw but is not called here; closeAccount (29) does call it; no other check in the file. Authentication of User not visible in this directory.

verdict.guard_found: canDelete (src/AccountService.java:9-11) returns a boolean that is discarded by the bare call at line 22; assertCanDelete (13-17) would throw but is never called in deleteAccount (only in closeAccount at line 29). No other check between the caller and accounts.remove(id) at line 23. Grep confirms no other references to deleteAccount/canDelete in the directory.
verdict.reason: deleteAccount at src/AccountService.java:20-23 calls canDelete(u, a) at line 22 as a bare statement, so its false result is ignored and accounts.remove(id) at line 23 runs for any caller, while the owner-or-admin check exists only in canDelete (9-11) and assertCanDelete (13-17), which this path never invokes. Caveat: the HTTP route, and whether User u is authenticated, are not in this directory; the attacker is an authenticated non-admin user, which is a real privilege gap rather than a role that already holds the power.

finding.claim: closeAccount fails differently for nonexistent vs. forbidden accounts, letting a non-admin enumerate account ids.
finding.source: Path parameter id of POST /accounts/{id}/close (AccountService.java:26-28). Precondition: authenticated non-admin user.
finding.sink: Observable error type/status differs: NullPointerException vs SecurityException, revealing account existence

trace.note: accounts.get(id) returns null when id does not exist
for non-admin, a.ownerId() dereferences null -> NullPointerException
for existing account owned by others, SecurityException thrown instead

finding.guards_checked: Owner check logic (AccountService.java:9-11) is correct for existing accounts; the gap is null handling. HTTP exception mapping not present in this directory, so observability of the difference is unverified.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check on this path is canDelete (AccountService.java:9-11), which is the function the candidate describes. It has no null guard, and nothing catches the NullPointerException or SecurityException before they propagate from closeAccount (lines 27-31). No HTTP exception mapping exists in this directory.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: accounts.get returns null for a missing id (AccountService.java:28), a non-admin then dereferences it at line 10 and gets an NPE, while an existing account owned by someone else throws SecurityException at line 15. Any authenticated non-admin reaches closeAccount, and no control blocks the difference. Whether that difference is observable to a client depends on HTTP error mapping, which is not in the available code, so the existence oracle cannot be confirmed (it would be refuted if both cases return the same generic 500).
